::: {.lead}
Today you write prompts and watch how the answer changes. Each experiment
has two parts. **Part A** is in an AI assistant on the lab computer.
**Part B** is on a simulator of the interactive lesson: on paper, scan its
QR code; on the screen, click its link. After each step, write your result
in its box. At the end, copy your key results into the table.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with a browser, and an AI assistant that the
  university allows (for example `copilot.microsoft.com` with your
  university account).
- **No lab computer today?** Do Part B on your phone. Part A works on the
  phone too, in an AI app or its website.
- **Never type personal data** (ID numbers, phone numbers, addresses) into
  an AI tool.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive lesson, every step has a check that answers
  at once.

## Experiment 1 · The three parts of a clear prompt

**The idea:** a clear **prompt** has three parts. The **task** says what the
AI must do. The **context** gives the facts of your situation. The
**format** sets the length, the form and the **tone** (for example polite or
friendly). Without context, the answer is general; without format, it can be
far too long.

**Aim:** see what each part of a prompt adds to the answer.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In an AI assistant**
:::

1. Send a prompt with a task only: *Write a short message to my study
   group.* Read the answer. Does it say the day and the place?

   {{< record "The day and the place in the answer? …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **No.** The answer is general, for example "Hi everyone, let's meet
   soon to study." The AI does not know your situation: the context is
   missing.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   You send only a task: "Write a short message to my study group." What is
   the answer like?

   - [x] general, without the day or the place

     Why: Without context, the AI does not know your situation.

   - [ ] exactly right, with the day and the place

     Why: The AI cannot know facts that you did not give it.

   - [ ] empty: the AI needs all three parts to answer

     Why: The AI answers, but in a general way.
   :::

2. Start a new chat. Send the full prompt: *Write a short message to my
   study group. We meet on Tuesday at 2 p.m. in the library to study for
   the Excel quiz. Write 3 friendly sentences for our group chat.*

   {{< record "The answer has … (day, time, place, how many sentences)" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good answer: three friendly sentences with **Tuesday**, **2 p.m.**,
   **the library** and **the Excel quiz**. The context gave the facts, and
   the format gave three friendly sentences. Read it before you send it.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Sort the parts of the full prompt.

   Task
   :   Write a short message to my study group.

       Why: It says what the AI must do.

   Context
   :   We meet on Tuesday at 2 p.m. in the library.

       Why: It gives the facts of your situation.

   :   We study for the Excel quiz.

       Why: Another fact of your situation.

   Format
   :   Write 3 friendly sentences for our group chat.

       Why: It sets the length, the form and the tone.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-02/sims/prompt-builder.html" poster="../../week-02/sims/prompt-builder.png" title="Prompt Builder: task, context and format" >}}

3. In **Prompt Builder**, add the blocks one by one and send each time:
   the task, then the context, then the format. What is the answer like
   with the task and the context, but no format?

   {{< record "Task + context, no format: the answer is …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Far too long:** the facts are right, but the answer is a long
   paragraph. With the format (3 polite sentences), it becomes short and
   clear.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   In Prompt Builder, which blocks give a clear, short, correct message?

   - [x] task + context + format

     Why: The task says what to write, the context gives the facts, the format makes it short and polite.

   - [ ] task + context

     Why: The facts are right, but the answer is far too long: add the format.

   - [ ] task + format + "My student ID is 2026123456."

     Why: No facts of the situation, and an ID number is personal data.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · Improve the answer with follow-up prompts

**The idea:** a **follow-up prompt** makes the last answer better, in the
same chat: *Make it shorter.*, *Make it a list of 3.*, *Write it for
students.* One short follow-up changes one thing. The AI remembers the last
answer only in the same chat: a new chat starts with nothing.

**Aim:** change an answer step by step, and see where follow-ups work.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In an AI assistant**
:::

1. In the chat of Experiment 1 · Step 2, send two follow-ups, one after the
   other: *Make it shorter.* and then *Translate it into Arabic.* What
   changed each time?

   {{< record "After the first … ; after the second …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The first follow-up made the message **shorter**; the second one put it
   **in Arabic**. The facts (Tuesday, 2 p.m., the library) stayed the same:
   each follow-up changed one thing.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   You send "Make it shorter." in the same chat. What does the AI change?

   - [x] the length: the facts stay the same

     Why: One short follow-up changes one thing of the last answer.

   - [ ] the facts: it writes about a new topic

     Why: The follow-up asked only for a shorter text.

   - [ ] nothing: follow-ups work only in a new chat

     Why: Follow-ups work in the same chat, where the AI has the last answer.
   :::

2. Start a **new chat** and send only: *Make it shorter.* What happens?

   {{< record "In a new chat, the AI …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The AI does not know what to make shorter: it asks for the text, or it
   writes something general. A new chat starts with nothing, so write
   follow-ups in the same chat.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Why does "Make it shorter." not work in a new chat?

   - [x] A new chat starts with nothing: the AI has no answer to change.

     Why: The AI remembers the last answer only in the same chat.

   - [ ] The prompt is too short for the AI.

     Why: Short follow-ups work well in the same chat.

   - [ ] The AI is busy with the old chat.

     Why: The new chat simply does not have the old answer.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-02/sims/follow-up.html" poster="../../week-02/sims/follow-up.png" title="Follow-up Chat: make the answer better" >}}

3. In **Follow-up Chat**, reach every goal of the simulator (3 tips, for
   students, a list, short) with follow-up prompts. Which follow-ups did
   you use?

   {{< record "My follow-ups" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   For example *Write it for university students.*, *Make it a list of 3
   tips.* and *Make each tip short, under 10 words.*: one change in each
   follow-up.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   What does each follow-up of Follow-up Chat change? Sort them.

   Who it is for
   :   Write it for university students.

       Why: It changes the readers of the text.

   The form
   :   Make it a list of 3 tips.

       Why: A paragraph becomes a list.

   The length
   :   Make each tip short, under 10 words.

       Why: The tips become shorter.

   :   Add more details.

       Why: The tips become longer.

   The language
   :   Translate it into Arabic.

       Why: The same tips in another language.
   :::

## Experiment 3 · Fix a weak prompt

**The idea:** a weak prompt misses a part: the task, the context or the
format. Find what is missing, and add it. A prompt never has personal data,
such as a phone number or an ID number.

**Aim:** turn a weak prompt into a clear one.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In an AI assistant**
:::

1. The weak prompt is *Write a notice.* Make it clear for this situation:
   the computer lab of the college is closed on Thursday 20 November for
   repairs. Add a context and a format, send it and read the answer.

   {{< record "My clear prompt" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good prompt, for example: *Write a notice for the notice board of our
   college. The computer lab is closed on Thursday 20 November for
   repairs. Use 3 short, polite sentences.* It has a task, a context and a
   format, and the answer has the date and the reason.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which prompt is clear?

   - [x] Write a notice for our college: the computer lab is closed on Thursday 20 November for repairs. Use 3 short, polite sentences.

     Why: It has a task, a context and a format.

   - [ ] Write a notice. Make it very, very good.

     Why: "Very good" is not a format, and there are no facts.

   - [ ] The computer lab is closed on Thursday 20 November.

     Why: It gives a fact, but no task and no format.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-02/sims/prompt-doctor.html" poster="../../week-02/sims/prompt-doctor.png" title="Prompt Doctor: what is missing?" >}}

2. In **Prompt Doctor**, find what is missing in each of the five weak
   prompts, then choose the better prompt. Which prompt has nothing
   missing?

   {{< record "The prompt with nothing missing" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   *Sum up this text about healthy food in 3 bullet points for my
   classmates*: a task (sum up), a context (a text about healthy food, for
   classmates) and a format (3 bullet points).
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   In Prompt Doctor, "Make 5 slides for my talk." What is missing?

   - [x] the context: the topic and the audience of the talk

     Why: The AI does not know what the talk is about, or who listens.

   - [ ] the task

     Why: "Make 5 slides" is the task.

   - [ ] nothing

     Why: Without the topic, the AI can only write general slides.
   :::
